title: Beatrix and the Debt
premise: Hazel Kavanagh, a private security contractor haunted by a botched extraction that killed his team, is approached by a stranger claiming Hazel once saved his life—a favor Hazel has no memory of. The stranger's 'repayment' is an ultimatum: infiltrate the covert training network that manufactured operators like Hazel and burn it down before it brokers a deal at an upcoming international security summit. As Hazel descends into the network's hierarchy, he discovers the stranger is its founder testing whether his creation can be unmade, and that the 'incident' was engineered to break him into compliance. In the end, Hazel exposes the network at the summit itself, choosing found family over survival, and finally sleeps through the night.
about_author: Mara Sterling is the pen name of a former risk analyst who spent a decade writing threat assessments for clients she was never allowed to name. She lives off-grid in coastal Maine, where she writes thrillers about people who know too much and trust too little.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Insomniac contractor Hazel Kavanagh works a forgettable protection detail when a stranger, Elias Voss, saves him from an ambush and claims Hazel saved him first—years ago, in a place Hazel can't remember. The debt is 'owed with interest.' Emotional beat: unease; the past Hazel buried has knocked on his door.

chapters.title: Interest Accrued
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Voss reveals the interest: infiltrate Meridian Group, the black-site training program that built Hazel and erased the memory of his time there, before it finalizes contracts at the Geneva summit. Refusal means the ambush was only a warning. Emotional beat: dread hardening into reluctant resolve as Hazel digs up his own redacted file.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Using forged credentials, Hazel penetrates Meridian's Vienna office and finds trainee files—including his own, stamped ASSET RETAINED. He meets June Okafor, a Meridian analyst who suspects the summit deal funds something monstrous. Emotional beat: vertigo; every certainty about his identity cracks open.

chapters.title: The Handler's Smile
chapters.summary: POV June. June covers for Hazel during a security sweep, torn between loyalty to the institution that rescued her from poverty and the evidence of what it sells. She agrees to feed him access codes. Emotional beat: complicity and awakening—the first thread of found family.

chapters.title: What the Incident Was For
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Hazel recovers suppressed footage: his team's deaths were staged by Meridian to traumatize him into deeper obedience. Grief curdles into fury. He realizes Voss knew all along. Emotional beat: betrayal atop grief; the mission stops being a debt and becomes vengeance.

chapters.title: Convergence
chapters.summary: POV Hazel and June (alternating). Racing the summit timeline, they extract Meridian's client ledger, but June is flagged as a leak and must go dark, sheltering with Hazel's estranged sister's family—the closest thing he has to home. Emotional beat: fragile trust; two broken people building something worth protecting.

chapters.title: The Founder's Face
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Confronting Voss, Hazel learns the truth: Voss founded Meridian and orchestrated everything—including the favor—to see if his finest product could choose to destroy its maker. Voss offers Hazel partnership: power instead of exposure. Emotional beat: temptation; corruption offered as salvation.

chapters.title: Summit Eve
chapters.summary: POV June. Meridian captures June and uses her as bait, forcing Hazel to trade the ledger for her life. He walks into the trap knowing it's a trap, carrying a dead-man's-switch upload keyed to the summit's mainframe. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen freely—the opposite of everything Meridian trained into him.

chapters.title: Burn the Network
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Inside the summit, Hazel triggers the upload, broadcasting Meridian's ledger to every delegate and press feed while fighting through Voss's operatives. He spares Voss, leaving him to face the collapse of his empire publicly. Emotional beat: cathartic climax; the fire is literal, digital, and moral at once.

chapters.title: Sleeping Through the Night
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Weeks later, testifying under immunity, Hazel visits June recovering in Lisbon, where his sister's kids have adopted them both as uncle and aunt. The nightmares fade—not gone, but quiet. Emotional beat: resolution; survival was the price, but family is what it bought.
